rv.q: The best musical based on American history since “Hamilton”.
Taub’s show is a triumph, with an enthralling plot, moving emotional moments and exceptional music and lyricism.
Shaina Taub (Book, Music, and Lyrics) has created a highly entertaining, powerfully sounding musical that will surely delight most audiences.
Stirring and powerful, the production feels eerily current because of today’s political discussions around voting and Taub’s sharp framing of a story that has driving music and anthemic lyrics.
“Suffs” takes the story out of the history books and onto the stage with flesh, heart and soul.
The all-female cast is top-to-bottom outstanding, with pure intensity from Keleher and sly regality Ramirez especially.
This all-female musical is a fast-paced and often breathtaking theatrical event.
Despite being written only a few years back, the show is in many ways a good, old-fashioned musical. It follows a tried and true structure and utilizes common platitudes of musical theater.
In today’s political climate, its message feels less like a history lesson, and more like a call to action.
“Suffs” is so energetic, enthusiastic and forward-moving it’s tough not to be utterly charmed by it all.
The production is amazing, with strong vocals and acting by all involved.
It’s a thrill to hear a large cast composed entirely of female and queer voices.

Although the subject matter is very important and the performances are full-out, the show grinds to a halt over and over again with scenes where a character says she can’t fight any more and then another character convinces her (in close harmony) to keep fighting.
"Suffs" feels somewhat incomplete. The musical acknowledges racial tensions within the movement, but its treatment of Black characters and their experience is cursory and underdeveloped.
That’s not the case with “Suffs,” which marches on as a skillfully crafted, perhaps slightly too streamlined pop history lesson.
The Black suffragists who appear in "Suffs" serve as plot devices more often than not.
There’s a blandness to Taub’s score, and yes, I know it won the 2024. Tony.

cn.t: Critics find this Tony-winning suffrage musical timely and well-crafted, with strong performances and harmonies, though some note it takes a workmanlike, educational approach that prioritizes historical detail over dramatic flair.
